name: Fertiliser supply
summary: Egyptian urea at $535 a tonne after gas cuts; Gulf nitrogen exports depend on an impeded Strait of Hormuz
state: Egyptian granular urea export prices reached $535 a tonne in November, about 17% above September's $457, after gas deliveries to producers were cut from 1 Nov (UkrAgroConsult, 10 Nov). Gulf urea exports rely on the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran restricts passage; Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on 16 Nov the southern passage had been mined (Shafaq News). The rise is below the 30% three-month Watch line and no export bans by several major exporters were found as of 27 Nov, so Watch holds on the impeded Gulf route.
for_you: Farmers buying nitrogen fertiliser for the next season and food importers are most exposed; higher fertiliser costs tend to reduce application rates and feed into crop prices the following year.
rubric_hit: Watch: Gulf export route impeded; Egyptian urea +17% since Sept, below the +30% three-month line

sources.title: UkrAgroConsult — Egyptian urea prices rise to $535 per ton amid gas supply restrictions
Shafaq News — IRGC ties six tanker incidents to mined Hormuz

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
